notes: Add meaningful accessibility regressions to the existing browser harness: Tab to /start/ disclosure buttons, press Enter and Space, assert content visibility and aria-expanded; assert both bulk controls work by keyboard.
At320 viewport open/close the mobile Menu with Enter, assert aria-expanded changes with visible navigation, then Tab through links and back out; retain an obvious focus indicator.

Select Other amount on /fundraising/ without submitting: assert the numeric input accessible name is Donation amount, instruction is associated, focus moves to it, and document scrollWidth does not exceed clientWidth.

Scan representative locally rendered pages and revealed states with pinned axe-core, including wcag2a,wcag2aa,wcag21a,wcag21aa,wcag22aa tags; save violations and incomplete checks as CI artifacts; use fake Stripe/captcha data rather than contacting real payment APIs.

Test invalid forms locally with synthetic data: verify each error is linked to its field and correction guidance is announced; test corporate member select/file accessible names and contact name/email autocomplete tokens.
Assert every main page has a useful unique title and that template variables do not appear escaped or unresolved in titles; inspect document titles with a screen reader.
Check badge images manually: informative badge text needs equivalent alt; purely decorative badges use empty alt; linked badges need the link purpose expressed in their accessible name.

Before sign-off, run NVDA with Firefox or Chrome on Windows and VoiceOver with Safari on macOS/iOS: navigate landmarks/headings, activate disclosures/menu, hear donation amount name/instructions and corporate fields, review error announcements and badge alternatives; record actual announcements and versions.

The report score and grade are heuristic prioritization measures, not WCAG conformance proof. Automated checks, limited browser states and source inspection leave screen-reader behavior and third-party checkout unverified.

Re-scan affected pages after each fix; run the representative browser/axe regression set for every PR touching templates, JavaScript or styles, and repeat the scoped production crawl following deployment.
